note: Priors of the stochastic scenario engine (tests/sim/models/scenario_engine.py). SYNTH = synthesized realistic placeholder for planning, NOT a fact. Same leaf schema as params.json plus 'dist'. See docs/SIM-SCENARIOS.md.
base_dist_note: Contour-specific priors (SYNTH) that replace the min/typ/max triangle of a params.json entry: air-to-ground LOS exponent close to free space; flight power around 24 dBm of a 28 dBm PA; small non-RF loss floor; moderate loss bursts; LOS air-to-ground Rician K around 10 dB; a decent 5 A supply cable.

hw.description: Nonlinear hardware of the AIR TX (OpenIPC WiFiLink2, RunCam RTL8812EU) and of the GS RX (RTL8812AU on Pi 5): PA compression, EVM floor, thermal derating, supply sag, AGC saturation, desense sources, antenna losses.
assumptions: Rapp AM-AM curve (smoothness p), EVM^2 = floor + (k*amplitude error)^2, SNR_eff = 1/(1/SNR + EVM^2) (INF, textbook)
Adapter thermal = first-order RC (Rth, tau) with derating above a start temperature and shutdown with hysteresis (INF)
TX output droops when the AIR supply is below a knee: k1*dV + k2*dV^2 dB (INF shape, SYNTH coefficients)
ELRS 900 MHz and the Multi 2.4 GHz module reach the 5 GHz receiver only via harmonics/intermod/ADC overload: one lumped coupling loss each, duty-cycled (INF)
Antenna losses = pattern null + polarisation mismatch + body shadow, persistent for ~tens of seconds (INF)

pa_p1db_out_dbm.note: output-referred 1 dB compression point of the AIR PA. SRC docs.openipc.org lists 28 dBm (FCC) as the rated power of WiFiLink2; P1dB itself is not published

pa_rapp_p.note: Rapp smoothness: 1.5 soft knee .. 4 hard knee (shape prior, SYNTH)

evm_floor_db.note: linear EVM floor (phase noise, IQ imbalance, DAC); 802.11 mandates only a ceiling per MCS

evm_comp_coeff.note: scale of the compression amplitude error in EVM (SYNTH)

evm_temp_db_per_c.note: EVM floor degradation per degree above 25 C (SYNTH)

air_rth_c_per_w.note: case-to-ambient thermal resistance of the WiFiLink2 radio incl. heatsink and fan (fan 25/30 g is SRC-listed per docs/SIM-BLOCKERS.md, Rth unknown)

air_tau_s.note: thermal time constant of the radio + heatsink

air_diss_frac.note: share of DC input power dissipated as heat (the rest is RF out); INF from PA efficiency 5..30 %

air_board_heat_w.note: SoC + sensor heat sharing the radio's heat path (SSC338Q + IMX415)

air_ambient_rise_c.note: airframe interior temperature rise above outside air (SYNTH)

thermal_derate_start_c.note: junction temperature where the driver starts to reduce TX power (RTL thermal tracking, threshold unknown)

thermal_derate_db_per_c.note: TX power reduction per degree above the start (SYNTH)

thermal_shutdown_c.note: thermal shutdown threshold (parameter; datasheet value not read)

thermal_hyst_c.note: hysteresis before TX resumes after shutdown (SYNTH)

air_bec_v.note: voltage the BEC delivers to the VTX (DC 9-22 V input, BEC recommended: SRC docs.openipc.org)

air_supply_r_ohm.note: AIR supply path resistance (BEC output, wire, connector) seen by the TX current pulse

air_supply_ripple_v.note: BEC ripple / noise std per slice (ESC and motor load)

tx_sag_knee_v.note: supply below which the PA output droops

tx_sag_k1_db_per_v.note: linear sag coefficient (power ~ V^2 gives ~3.5 dB/V near 5 V)

tx_sag_k2_db_per_v2.note: quadratic sag coefficient (hard droop near brown-out)

rx_agc_knee_dbm.note: received level where the GS ADC/AGC starts to saturate (too close to the AIR TX)

rx_agc_slope.note: SNR loss per dB above the knee (SYNTH)

elrs900_present.note: ELRS RX on 900 MHz is in the AIR contour (user fact); at the GS the external TX module is the source

elrs900_tx_dbm.note: ELRS 900 MHz TX module power at the GS (100 mW..1 W); model of the module unknown

elrs900_coupling_db.note: EFFECTIVE in-band-equivalent coupling of the 900 MHz module into the 5.8 GHz receiver: harmonics/intermod, out-of-band rejection and antenna isolation lumped (very high loss expected; the tail is the risk)

elrs900_duty.note: share of time the module radiates (packet rate x airtime), SYNTH

multi24_present.note: TX12 MKII internal Multi module: 2.4 GHz may be switched on at the GS (user fact; protocol unknown)

multi24_tx_dbm.note: Multi module output power (CC2500/ELRS 2.4); the exact module is unknown

multi24_coupling_db.note: EFFECTIVE in-band-equivalent coupling of the 2.4 GHz Multi module into the 5.8 GHz receiver incl. antenna proximity and out-of-band rejection

multi24_duty.note: share of time the Multi module radiates

usb3_present_prob.note: probability that a noisy USB3 path (cable/port/SSD) is active during a session

usb3_noise_dbm.note: broadband USB3 noise reaching the 5.8 GHz input (USB3 noise is mainly 2.4 GHz; effect on 5.8 is unverified)

ant_null_prob.note: share of time the antenna pattern is in a null

ant_pol_max_deg.note: maximum polarisation tilt between the AIR and GS antennas

ant_body_prob.note: share of time the operator's body/airframe shadows an antenna

ant_persist_s.note: how long an orientation state persists

soc_rise_c.note: Pi 5 SoC temperature rise above ambient with decode load and the cooler fitted (no cooler is worse)

soc_soft_limit_c.note: temperature where the Pi 5 caps the ARM clock (vcgencmd get_throttled bit 3/2)

throttle_decode_factor.note: decode-time multiplier while the clock is capped

calibration.measure: AIR conducted/radiated power vs commanded txpower (power meter or SDR), and EVM per MCS
calibration.command: iw dev wlan0 set txpower fixed <mBm> at 17..28 dBm; capture with a spectrum analyser/power meter
calibration.tool: power meter or SDR + 30 dB attenuator
calibration.how: Fit the Rapp curve to Pout vs Pin: P1dB = the point where gain is 1 dB lower; EVM from the analyser at MCS 1 and 7

calibration.measure: adapter case temperature vs time at flight TX power in the closed enclosure (thermal camera or NTC on the heatsink)
calibration.command: run TX at flight power 30 min; log vtx temperature (majestic/telemetry) every 5 s; repeat at 40 C ambient (warm box)
calibration.how: Rth = (Tss - Tamb)/P; tau = time to 63 % of the rise; derate/shutdown from the first power drop seen by the power meter

calibration.measure: VTX 5 V rail during TX bursts (scope on the BEC output)
calibration.command: scope on the VTX 5 V pad while txpower steps; lab supply stepped 5.0->4.2 V to measure output power
calibration.tool: scope, adjustable lab supply, power meter
calibration.how: R = dV/dI at the burst; sag coefficients from Pout vs rail voltage

calibration.measure: GS RX SNR/PER vs received level at very short range (conducted with attenuators)
calibration.command: AIR TX -> variable attenuator 0..60 dB -> GS RX; log PER in wfb-cli gs
calibration.how: knee = level where PER starts to rise as attenuation decreases

calibration.measure: GS PER with the ELRS 900 MHz module and the Multi 2.4 GHz module transmitting next to the dongle, and with/without USB3 devices
calibration.command: fixed link at ~10 dB margin; switch each module/USB3 device on and off; wfb-cli gs loss counters
calibration.tool: attenuators, the real TX12 and modules
calibration.how: dSNR (dB) at a known received level gives the noise rise: coupling = interferer power at the source minus the implied in-band-equivalent power

calibration.measure: RSSI distribution while rotating the airframe / walking (antenna nulls, polarisation, body shadow)
calibration.command: log RSSI per antenna at fixed 100 m LOS while rotating through attitudes for 10 min
calibration.how: histogram of RSSI deficit vs the maximum; autocorrelation time = persistence

calibration.measure: Pi 5 SoC temperature and get_throttled during decode at 30 C ambient
calibration.command: vcgencmd measure_temp; vcgencmd get_throttled every 5 s for 30 min under the real GS load
calibration.how: rise = SoC temp - ambient; decode factor from GStreamer latency before/after capping

proc.description: Slow stochastic processes: noise-floor drift and shocks, shadowing, component ageing.
assumptions: noise-floor excess = Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift + Poisson shocks (lognormal size, exponential decay) (INF)
log-normal shadowing as an AR(1) process in dB (INF)
ageing linear in operating hours (INF)

nf_ou_sigma_db.note: stationary std of the slow noise-floor drift

shock_rate_per_h.note: Poisson rate of interference shocks (ESC, neighbour transmitters)

shadow_sigma_db.note: log-normal shadowing sigma (3..8 dB outdoors is a textbook range)

age_hours.note: operating hours of the radios at the time of the flight

calibration.measure: noise floor over a 1 h log on the ground and in the air (iw survey dump / wfb-cli noise)
calibration.command: iw dev wlan0 survey dump every 2 s for 1 h; ESC on/off
calibration.how: OU sigma/tau from the autocorrelation of the log; shocks = excursions > 3 sigma

calibration.measure: RSSI vs time for a moving aircraft on a fixed-range arc
calibration.command: fly/drive a fixed-radius arc, log RSSI
calibration.how: sigma = std of the detrended RSSI in dB; tau = decorrelation time

calibration.measure: same link measured with a new unit and an old one (batch of hours)
calibration.command: compare sensitivity (PER at fixed attenuation) and Pout of units with different logged hours
calibration.how: slope per 1000 h; hours from the unit log

ext.description: External factors: ambient temperature, sun load, channel clash / interference episodes.
assumptions: ambient temperature normal around the flight day; sun load adds to the airframe interior (SYNTH)
clash episodes = two-state chain at slice level (Gilbert-style), INR over the noise floor while on

ambient_c.note: outside air temperature of the session

solar_rise_c.note: extra heating of the enclosures by direct sun

clash_rate_per_h.note: start rate of interference episodes on the channel (neighbour FPV/AP)

calibration.measure: channel occupancy at the flying site (survey of the channel over 1 h, spectrum scan)
calibration.command: iw dev wlan0 survey dump / channel-scan.sh repeatedly at the site
calibration.how: episodes = intervals where busy time rises above threshold; INR from the busy-noise level

calibration.measure: ambient and sun load of the planned flight (thermometer in the sun/shade, enclosure surface)
calibration.command: thermometer log; IR thermometer on the closed enclosure after 10 min in the sun
calibration.how: distribution over the planned season/location

vid.description: Video encoder behaviour that stresses the air interface.
assumptions: majestic delivers more than the configured bitrate in bursts (overshoot), with a periodic IDR (GOP)

bitrate_overshoot.note: mean encoded bitrate / configured bitrate (rate control overshoot)

gop_s.note: IDR period in seconds (majestic default unknown)

calibration.measure: actual encoder bitrate and IDR period from a capture (tcpdump on the wfb UDP port / majestic log)
calibration.command: tcpdump -i lo udp port 5600 for 5 min; bitrate per 1 s; IDR spacing from the stream
calibration.how: overshoot = mean/config; GOP = IDR spacing

inj.description: Injection path (wfb_tx -> driver queue): random EBUSY, finite queue (M/M/1/K) and rate cap.
assumptions: M/M/1/K blocking at the TX queue with utilisation rho = offered packets / min(air capacity, rate cap) (INF)
an I-frame burst arrives within one frame period and overflows the queue (INF)

queue_pkts.note: driver/socket TX queue length in packets

rate_cap_pps.note: maximum injection rate the driver/USB path sustains (packets per second)

ebusy_prob.note: per-frame random EBUSY/ENOBUFS probability even without overload

calibration.measure: maximum injection rate and drop counters with an overloaded wfb_tx
calibration.command: wfb_tx with bitrate above the air capacity; count send errors (strace -c / wfb_tx stats)
calibration.how: rate_cap = max sustained pps; ebusy = errors per frame at low load

usb.description: GS USB/power: PSU sag, USB drop hazard vs margin, re-enumeration, Pi 5 current-limit trip.
assumptions: hazard = base * exp(-V margin/Vs) * exp(-I margin/Is) (INF shape)
Pi 5 limit 0.6 A vs 1.6 A is power_model.usb_budget_a (SRC raspberrypi docs); trip behaviour is an assumption
peak currents from power_model (tx_peak_factor)

cable_r_ohm.note: extra resistance of the dongle USB cable and connector (thin cables, SRC wfb-ng warns about them)

drop_rate_per_h.note: spontaneous USB disconnect rate at ample margins

drop_v_scale.note: e-fold voltage margin of the drop hazard

drop_i_scale_a.note: e-fold current margin of the drop hazard

reenum_fail_prob.note: probability that the adapter does not come back without a replug

gs_tx_burst_hz.note: TX burst rate of the GS adapter (uplink MAVLink/RC override, keepalive)

pi5_trip_tol.note: tolerance above the documented limit before the Pi 5 trips

pi5_trip_off_s.note: port-off time after a current-limit trip

pi5_trip_latch_n.note: consecutive trips after which the port stays off until a power cycle (assumption)

calibration.measure: USB current and 5 V rail at the Pi during the real GS load (TX bursts), with a 3 A and a 5 A PSU, usb_max_current_enable 0/1
calibration.command: USB inline meter + scope on the 5 V; dmesg -w for over-current; vcgencmd get_throttled
calibration.how: trip tolerance/off time from dmesg timestamps; cable R from dV/dI

calibration.measure: USB disconnect events in a 24 h soak (dmesg 'USB disconnect', udev remove)
calibration.command: journalctl -k -f | grep -i usb for 24 h at two margins (5 A PSU vs 3 A PSU)
calibration.how: rate vs margin gives base and scales; time to return gives the re-enum distribution

bringup.description: Device bring-up failures: USB probe, firmware load, monitor-mode set, injection start; retries with exponential backoff.
assumptions: each stage is a Bernoulli trial per attempt; a failed attempt costs a timeout plus backoff base*factor^(i-1); after max attempts the stage fails (INF)

max_attempts.note: retry count assumed for the bring-up service (a design choice; the repo has no retry loop yet)

usb_probe_fail_p.note: per-attempt failure probability: USB enumeration (descriptor read timeouts, error -71)

usb_probe_timeout_s.note: time lost by a failed attempt: USB enumeration (descriptor read timeouts, error -71)

usb_probe_ok_s.note: time of a successful attempt: USB enumeration (descriptor read timeouts, error -71)

fw_timeout_s.note: time lost by a failed attempt: firmware/driver init

fw_ok_s.note: time of a successful attempt: firmware/driver init

monitor_fail_p.note: per-attempt failure probability: iw set type monitor (busy: NetworkManager, rfkill)

monitor_timeout_s.note: time lost by a failed attempt: iw set type monitor (busy: NetworkManager, rfkill)

monitor_ok_s.note: time of a successful attempt: iw set type monitor (busy: NetworkManager, rfkill)

inj_start_fail_p.note: per-attempt failure probability: first injection test (EBUSY at start)

inj_start_timeout_s.note: time lost by a failed attempt: first injection test (EBUSY at start)

inj_start_ok_s.note: time of a successful attempt: first injection test (EBUSY at start)

calibration.measure: 50 cold boots / hot-plugs: stage outcomes and durations from the logs
calibration.command: loop: power-cycle the dongle (uhubctl or relay) 50 times; log dmesg, iw set monitor exit codes, first wfb_tx send result
calibration.tool: uhubctl or a relay, shell loop
calibration.how: failure fraction per stage = p; mean durations = timeouts/ok times

timing.description: Time: clock drift, scheduler jitter, queue (latency) creep, stalls, packet reordering.
assumptions: queue creep = max(0, ppm) drift of the producer vs the sink until the leaky queue drops; stalls add a backlog that decays slowly (INF)
scheduler jitter = lognormal + rare exponential spikes (INF)

clock_ppm.note: frame-clock mismatch between the VTX encoder and the GS display/sink

ntp_step_rate_per_h.note: rate of wall-clock steps (NTP/chrony) on the GS or host

sched_jitter_median_ms.note: median wake-up latency of the GS pipeline threads

sched_spike_prob.note: probability of a scheduling spike per sample

sched_spike_mean_ms.note: mean spike length (CPU contention, decode load)

queue_max_ms.note: size of the leaky queue/jitter buffer where frames are dropped

stall_rate_per_h.note: pipeline stall (decoder hiccup, GC, USB) rate

stall_backlog_ms.note: mean backlog added by a stall

reorder_delay_ms.note: mean extra wait for a reordered packet

calibration.measure: glass-to-glass latency over 30 min (LED + photodiode or phone slow motion), GStreamer queue levels, decoder stalls
calibration.command: protocol: python3 tests/sim/models/latency_budget.py protocol; GST_DEBUG=GST_TRACER:7 latency tracer; watch latency drift over 30 min
calibration.how: creep slope = ppm; stalls from latency steps

calibration.measure: chrony/NTP step log of the host over a week; wfb_rx reorder counters
calibration.command: chronyc tracking/journal; wfb-cli gs counters
calibration.how: step rate and size from the journal; reorder from out-of-order seq counters

gpio.description: Mechanical button (GPIO) bounce, glitches and the timing of the REAL algorithm of gs/button.sh; RP1 specifics for Pi 5.
assumptions: gs/button.sh button_action: gpiomon -r waits for the first rising edge, sleep 0.05, gpioget must read 1, uptime in centiseconds (cut -d ' ' -f1 /proc/uptime | tr -d .), gpiomon -f waits for the first falling edge, uptime again; < 200 cs = single, >= 200 = long (REPO gs/button.sh)
contact bounce = alternating transitions with exponential gaps, settles at the final level; release bounce scaled by a factor (INF)
RP1 (Pi 5 GPIO behind PCIe) adds interrupt latency/jitter, may drop edges and has a hardware input filter; all values UNMEASURED

settle_s.note: sleep between the first rising edge and the level check

debounce_ms.note: kernel/libgpiod debounce period in use: 0 = none (gpiomon is called without a debounce option)

bounce_count_mean.note: mean number of bounce pairs on a press (tact switch: a few)

bounce_total_ms.note: mean total bounce duration of a press (typical tact switch 1..5 ms, worn: tens of ms)

glitch_rate_per_s.note: EMI glitch rate on the line (long wires near ESC/motors)

chatter_prob.note: probability that vibration briefly opens the contact during a long hold

single_hold_s.note: hold time of an intended short press

long_hold_mu_s.note: mean hold of an intended long press (operator)

long_hold_sigma_s.note: spread of the intended long hold

mon_start_ms.note: fork+exec+open latency of gpiomon (edges inside it are not seen)

get_ms.note: latency of gpioget until the level is sampled

uptime_ms.note: latency of the cut|tr pipeline reading /proc/uptime

exit_ms.note: gpiomon event delivery and exit latency

action_ms.note: execution time of the dispatched function before the loop re-arms

rp1_irq_latency_us.note: RP1 interrupt latency over PCIe added to every edge

rp1_edge_loss_prob.note: probability that an RP1 edge event is lost (coalescing)

rp1_filter_us.note: RP1 hardware input glitch filter (pulses shorter are ignored); 0 = off. Datasheet value not read

calibration.measure: press/release bounce and glitches on the real button with a scope or logic analyser (>= 100 presses), and the edge timestamps libgpiod sees (gpiomon -r -f --format for 100 presses)
calibration.command: logic analyser on the pin; in parallel gpiomon --num-events=0 --format='%e %s.%n' for 100 presses on a Pi 5 and a Radxa
calibration.how: bounce stats from the analyser; RP1 latency = libgpiod timestamp - analyser edge; lost edges = analyser edges - gpiomon edges

calibration.measure: real latencies of the button.sh loop: time between edge and uptime reading, and between exit and re-arm
calibration.command: bash -x with timestamps (PS4='+ $EPOCHREALTIME ') on button.sh on the Pi 5; 50 presses
calibration.how: differences between consecutive trace lines

calibration.measure: hold times of single and long presses by 3 operators (20 each)
calibration.command: log press durations with a logic analyser
calibration.how: lognormal/normal fit
